name: Critical minerals
summary: China extended its pause on new rare-earth export controls to 10 Jan 2027 on 9 Nov; April 2025 licensing still in force
state: China's commerce ministry said on 9 Nov that its suspension of new export controls on rare earths and related items, due to lapse on 10 Nov, is extended to 10 Jan 2027 (The Star; ThePrint). The extension lasts only two months and the April 2025 licensing requirements for seven rare earths remain in force, so Watch holds. No production stoppages outside China linked to export bans were found as of 11 Nov.
for_you: Rare earths and related minerals go into magnets for cars, wind turbines, electronics and defence equipment. Licensing delays mainly affect manufacturers; consumers tend to see effects later through product availability and prices.
rubric_hit: Licensing regime still in force with only a two-month pause on new controls: Watch line (licensing slowed)

sources.title: The Star — China extends suspension of rare earth export controls until January
ThePrint — China extends suspension of new rare earth controls until January

why: Rare earths, gallium, germanium and graphite are chokepoints for chips, EVs and defence — and China dominates processing.
drivers: Export controls, trade disputes, mine outages, stockpiling.

rubric.alert: Export bans in force that are causing reported production stoppages outside China.
rubric.watch: New export controls announced or licensing slowed.
rubric.normal: No new export restrictions in the past month.
